sections.title: Sound of ache
paragraphs: The letter name is (ache) /aʃ/. This letter makes no sound at all. It is always silent. You can hear this in (habiter) /a.bi.te/, which means to live, to reside. The word begins straight away with the vowel sound. This letter has zero sounds in modern speech.

sections.title: Pronunciation of ache
paragraphs: A silent letter is a letter that you write but do not say. Because this letter has no sound, your mouth does nothing special for it. Do not push any air from your throat. Do not move your tongue or your lips. Put a hand on your throat. You will feel no breath before the following vowel starts.

sections.title: Spelling of ache
paragraphs: This letter is always silent. It has no sound in words like (homme) /ɔm/. It is also completely silent in words like (héros) /e.ʁo/. You never say a breath sound when you see it in text. Simply read the rest of the word.

sections.title: Pitfalls with ache
paragraphs: Do not blow air when you see this letter. In English, you blow air out in hotel or home. In French, you never blow that air. Start cleanly with the vowel sound instead. Keep your throat quiet and relaxed.
